# 2 Kings Chapter 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 245r

---

**25:1** And-it-was in-the-ninth year of-his-reign [le-molkho], in-the-tenth month [ba-chodesh ha-'asiri], on-the-tenth of-the-month, Nevukhadnetstsar king of-Bavel came, he and-all his-army [cheylo], against Yerushalayim, and-he-encamped [vayichan] against-it and-built against-it a-siege-wall [dayeq] all-around [saviv].

**25:2** And-the-city came under-siege [ba-matsur] until the-eleventh year of-the-king Tsidqiyyahu.

**25:3** On-the-ninth of-the-month [ba-tish'ah la-chodesh], the-famine was-severe [vayechezaq ha-ra'av] in-the-city, and-there-was-no bread [lechem] for-the-people of-the-land.

**25:4** And-was-breached [vattibbaqq'a] the-city, and-all the-men of-war [anshey ha-milchamah] [fled] by-night [laylah] by-the-way of-the-gate between the-two-walls [beyn ha-chomotayim] which [is] by the-garden of-the-king [gan ha-melekh], and-the-Kasdim [were] against the-city all-around. And-he-went [vayyelekh] the-way of-the-Aravah.

**25:5** And-pursued [vayirdefu] the-army of-the-Kasdim after the-king and-overtook-him [vayassigu oto] in-the-plains [arvot] of-Yericho, and-all his-army was-scattered [nafetsu] from-upon-him.

**25:6** And-they-seized [vayitpesu] the-king and-brought-him-up to the-king of-Bavel at-Rivlah, and-they-spoke judgment [vayedabberu itto mishpat] with-him.

**25:7** And-the-sons of-Tsidqiyyahu they-slaughtered [shachatu] before-his-eyes [le-'eynayv], and-the-eyes of-Tsidqiyyahu he-blinded [iwwer], and-he-bound-him [vaya'asrehu] in-bronze [nechushtayim] and-brought-him to-Bavel.

**25:8** And-in-the-fifth month [ba-chodesh ha-chamishi], on-the-seventh of-the-month — it [was] the-nineteenth year of-the-king Nevukhadnetstsar king of-Bavel — came Nevuzar'adan, chief of-the-guard [rav tabachim], servant of-the-king of-Bavel, to-Yerushalayim.

**25:9** And-he-burned [vayisrof] the-house of-YHWH [beyt YHWH] and-the-house of-the-king [beyt ha-melekh] and-all the-houses of-Yerushalayim, and-every great house [beyt gadol] he-burned with-fire.

**25:10** And-the-walls of-Yerushalayim, all-around, the-army of-the-Kasdim which [was] with the-chief of-the-guard broke-down [natetsu].

**25:11** And-the-rest of-the-people [yeter ha-'am] who-remained [ha-nish'arim] in-the-city, and-the-deserters [ha-nofelim] who had-fallen-away [nafelu] to the-king of-Bavel, and-the-rest of-the-multitude [yeter he-hamon], Nevuzar'adan the-chief of-the-guard exiled [heglah].

**25:12** And-from-the-poorest of-the-land [u-middallat ha-arets] the-chief of-the-guard left-behind [hish'ir] vine-dressers [koremim] and-field-workers [yogevim].

**25:13** And-the-pillars [ha-'ammudim] of-bronze [ha-nechoshet] which [were] in-the-house of-YHWH, and-the-stands [ha-mekhonot] and-the-bronze sea [yam ha-nechoshet] which [was] in-the-house of-YHWH, the-Kasdim broke-in-pieces [shibru] and-carried their-bronze to-Bavel.

**25:14** And-the-pots [ha-sirot] and-the-shovels [ha-ya'im] and-the-snuffers [ha-mezammerot] and-the-dishes [ha-kappot] and-all the-vessels of-bronze [kley ha-nechoshet] with-which they-served [yesharetu], they-took.

**25:15** And-the-firepans [ha-machtot] and-the-bowls [ha-mizraqot] — what [was] gold, gold; and-what [was] silver, silver — the-chief of-the-guard took.

**25:16** The-two pillars, the-one sea, and-the-stands which Shelomoh had-made for-the-house of-YHWH — there-was-no weight [lo hayah mishqal] for-the-bronze of-all these vessels.

**25:17** Eighteen cubits [shemoneh esreh ammah] [was] the-height of-the-one pillar, and-a-capital [koteret] of-bronze [was] upon-it, and-the-height of-the-capital [was] three cubits, and-a-network [sevakhah] and-pomegranates [rimmonim] [were] upon the-capital all-around, all of-bronze. And-like-these had-the-second pillar, upon the-network.

**25:18** And-took the-chief of-the-guard Serayah the-chief priest [kohen ha-ro'sh] and-Tsefanyahu the-second priest [kohen mishneh] and-the-three keepers of-the-threshold [shomrey ha-saf].

**25:19** And-from the-city he-took one officer [saris] who was appointed [muqqad] over the-men of-war, and-five men from-those-who-see the-face of-the-king [mero'ey feney ha-melekh] who-were-found in-the-city, and-the-scribe of-the-commander of-the-army [sofer sar ha-tsava] who-mustered [ha-matsbi] the-people of-the-land, and-sixty men of-the-people of-the-land who-were-found in-the-city.

**25:20** And-took-them Nevuzar'adan the-chief of-the-guard and-brought-them to the-king of-Bavel at-Rivlah.

**25:21** And-struck-them [vayyakkem] the-king of-Bavel and-put-them-to-death [vayemitem] at-Rivlah in-the-land of-Chamat. And-was-exiled [vayyigel] Yehudah from-upon its-land ['admato].

**25:22** And-the-people who-remained in-the-land of-Yehudah, whom Nevukhadnetstsar king of-Bavel had-left, he-appointed [vayafqed] over-them Gedalyahu son of-Achiqam son of-Shaphan.

**25:23** And-heard all the-commanders of-the-armies [sarey ha-chayalim], they and-the-men, that the-king of-Bavel had-appointed Gedalyahu, and-they-came to Gedalyahu at-Mitspah: Yishma'el son of-Netanyahu and-Yochanan son of-Qareach and-Serayah son of-Tanchumet the-Netofati and-Ya'azanyahu son of-the-Ma'akhati, they and-their-men.

**25:24** And-swore [vayyishava'] to-them Gedalyahu and-to-their-men and-said to-them: Do-not fear [al tir'u] the-servants of-the-Kasdim. Dwell [shevu] in-the-land and-serve the-king of-Bavel, and-it-will-be-well [veyitav] with-you.

**25:25** And-it-was in-the-seventh month [ba-chodesh ha-shevi'i], Yishma'el son of-Netanyahu son of-Elishama, of-the-seed of-the-kingship [mi-zera' ha-melukhah], came, and-ten men with-him, and-they-struck [vayyakku] Gedalyahu and-he-died [vayyamot], and-the-Yehudim [Jews] and-the-Kasdim who-were with-him at-Mitspah.

**25:26** And-arose all the-people, from-small to-great, and-the-commanders of-the-armies, and-they-came [vayavo'u] to-Mitsrayim, for they-were-afraid [yar'u] of-the-Kasdim.

**25:27** And-it-was in-the-thirty and-seventh year of-the-exile [galut] of-Yehoyakhin king of-Yehudah, in-the-twelfth month [ba-chodesh ha-shenim 'asar], on-the-twenty and-seventh of-the-month, Evil-Merodakh [Evil Merodakh] king of-Bavel, in-the-year of-his-becoming-king [bi-shenat molkho], lifted-up [nasa] the-head [rosh] of-Yehoyakhin king of-Yehudah from-the-house of-imprisonment [mi-beyt kele].

**25:28** And-he-spoke to-him good-things [tovot] and-set [vayyitten] his-throne [kis'o] above the-thrones of-the-kings who [were] with-him in-Bavel.

**25:29** And-he-changed [ve-shinnah] his-garments of-imprisonment [bigdey kel'o], and-he-ate bread [lechem] before-him [le-fanayv] continually [tamid], all the-days of-his-life.

**25:30** And-his-allowance [aruchato], a-continual allowance [aruchat tamid], was-given to-him from the-king, the-matter of-a-day in-its-day [devar yom be-yomo], all the-days of-his-life.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "the famine was severe in the city":** The Hebrew *vayechezaq ha-ra'av* uses the verb *chazaq* (to be strong, severe). The famine is personified as a force — it grows strong while the city grows weak. Lamentations 4:9-10 provides the horrific details of what this famine produced.

**v.7 — "slaughtered his sons before his eyes, then blinded his eyes":** The sequence is deliberate and cruel: the last thing Zedekiah sees is the murder of his own sons. Then his eyes are destroyed. His final visual memory is of his children's deaths.

**v.9 — "he burned the house of YHWH":** *Beyt YHWH* — the house that Solomon built (1 Kings 6-7), that Josiah repaired (2 Kings 22), that contained the name of God. The three-word clause *vayisrof et-beyt YHWH* destroys in a breath what took chapters to construct.

**v.21 — "And Judah was exiled from upon its land":** The sentence *vayyigel Yehudah me-'al admato* is the Deuteronomistic history's final verdict. The word *adamah* (ground, soil) echoes God's original promise of land. What was given is now taken.

**vv.27-30 — Evil-Merodach lifts the head of Jehoiachin:** The idiom *nasa rosh* (lift the head) can mean either "to restore honor" or "to execute" (cf. Gen 40:13, 19). Here it means restoration. The book of Kings ends not with destruction but with this ambiguous gesture of grace — bread and a throne in exile. Not redemption. Not return. Just survival, and a flickering possibility.

*— EMET*
